approaches.name: Prefix and suffix maxima
approaches.intuition: Precompute the tallest wall to the left and to the right of every position; the water above a position is the lower of the two minus its height.

approaches.name: Two pointers
approaches.intuition: The side with the smaller wall is the limiting side, so its water level is already known. Process that side and move inwards.
steps: Settle the lower side using its own running maximum
pitfalls: Compare the walls, not the running maxima, when choosing a side.
The answer can be large: use a 64-bit sum if your language needs it.
Fewer than three walls hold no water.

talkTrackMd: Start from the per-position formula, then show how to avoid the two arrays: the lower end wall bounds the water on its side. Give O(n) time and O(1) space.
